steps.summary: Carved stone text reading 'KENT' on the cornice above the central section
Carved stone Latin text reading 'IVS EST ARS' and partially visible text 'REQVI' below the upper windows
Two fluted Ionic columns with volute capitals in pale stone supporting the structure
Neoclassical facade with red/brown brick walls and pale stone trim
Ornamental cornice with dentil molding and repeating geometric pattern across the top
Arched black wooden double doors with transom window above
Three rectangular windows with blue-tinted panes arranged symmetrically above the entrance
Pale stone panel or tablet below the central window
Rectangular stone plaques or decorative panels on either side of the central section
Dark wooden doors visible on the far left and right sides of the facade
Metal railing or gate visible at street level on the lower left
Small white sign or placard in the lower left corner
Stepped stone or brick entrance platform at base of facade

The carved stone text "KENT" (e1) on the cornice strongly suggests this building is named or located in Kent. The Latin motto "IVS EST ARS BONI ET AEQVI" (law is the art of goodness and fairness) is a classical legal maxim often used on courthouses, suggesting this is a civic/legal building. Combined with 'KENT' this points to Kent, Ohio, a city with historic civic architecture of this neoclassical style. The 'Book Return' sign visible near the entrance (e12) suggests this could actually be a library building, which fits with Kent, Ohio's civic district having Beaux-Arts/neoclassical public buildings from the early 20th century.
